_comment: PRODUCT CONFIG: same-night 2-VISIT ALERT tier. Optimized for FOLLOW-UP YIELD, not standalone purity (faint-fast 2v purity caps ~8% at ANY threshold -- base-rate wall, proven exhaustively; see THRESHOLD_DECISION.md / PHYSICAL_LEVERS_2V.md). Output = ranked follow-up packets (alerts.jsonl), NEVER a discovery claim. Pass to trail_state_link via --op-point. Differs from the discovery op: mfsnr relaxed 10->5 (measured at S=0.80: faint-fast completeness 1.7%->6.1% for false-link rate 0.12->3.4/field-night -- rankable, cappable volume), claim_tier=alert.
model_version: seg_v2 depth-4 (iter08) segmentation + focal-cutout CNN postproc
calibrated_on: 82 off-ecliptic injection fields, 2026-06, realistic ~34-min WFD same-night cadence; mfsnr sweep measure_nomfsnr.py (results/mfsnr_completeness_vs_lambda_S080.txt)
notes: DECIDED 2026-06-10 (ALERT_SWEEP_DECISION.md, real-night sweep band-box + NY2 night): default mfsnr>=5 with alerts_top_n=50/night. Measured operating points at S=0.80 (faint-fast bin SNR 2-10, rate>1 deg/day): mfsnr>=5 -> C=6.1%, lambda=3.4 false/field-night (dense-field UPPER bound; real nights measured 1-2 alerts/night); mfsnr>=7 -> C=3.9%, lambda=1.0; mfsnr>=10 -> C=1.7%, lambda=0.12. Alert tier accepts the higher false rate because alerts are RANKED (priorityScore) and CAPPED per night, and a 3rd observation confirms or kills each candidate ((FP)^N: 3v promotion measured 0 false). mfsnr=7 is the documented fallback knob if follow-up capacity saturates. NY2 regression intact at both settings.
